items.question: Northbridge walks Voss-Lindqvist through its methodology on a video call and hands over nothing in writing. Can what was said still be Confidential Information under the NDA?
items.answer:
The Northbridge NDA defines "Confidential Information" as all information disclosed by a Party to the other in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential [1].

The NDA also specifies that Confidential Information does not include information that the Recipient can show (a) is or becomes public other than through a breach of the Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Discloser's information; or (d) is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence [1].

Based on these terms, what was said during a video call could still be considered Confidential Information if it was disclosed in connection with the Purpose and would reasonably be understood to be confidential. However, the NDA does not explicitly state whether verbal disclosures are included in the definition of Confidential Information. The NDA only states that Confidential Information is disclosed in any form, but it does not clarify whether verbal communication alone is sufficient to qualify as Confidential Information.

items.question: Northbridge walks Voss-Lindqvist through its methodology on a video call and hands over nothing in writing. Can what was said still be Confidential Information under the NDA?
items.answer:
The Northbridge NDA defines "Confidential Information" in clause 2.2. It states that Confidential Information includes all information disclosed by a Party (the "Discloser") to the other (the "Recipient") in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential [1].

The Northbridge NDA also specifies that Confidential Information does not include information that the Recipient can show (a) is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Discloser's information; or (d) is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence [1].

Based on the definition provided in the Northbridge NDA, what was said during a video call could still be considered Confidential Information if it meets the criteria outlined in clause 2.2. items.question: Northbridge gives Voss-Lindqvist some market figures under the NDA, and Voss-Lindqvist later gets the same figures from an industry consultant who is free to pass them on. Is Voss-Lindqvist still bound by the NDA as to those figures?
items.answer:
The Northbridge NDA defines "Confidential Information" as all information disclosed by one party to the other in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential [3]. It also states that Confidential Information does not include information that the Recipient can show (a) is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Discloser's information; or (d) is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence [3].

In this scenario, Voss-Lindqvist received market figures from Northbridge under the NDA. Later, Voss-Lindqvist obtained the same figures from an industry consultant who is free to pass them on. Based on the definition of Confidential Information in the Northbridge NDA, if the figures were lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence, then they would not be considered Confidential Information under the NDA. The documents do not specify whether the industry consultant had a duty of confidence, but they do state that the Recipient is not bound by the NDA if the information was lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence [3].

Therefore, if the industry consultant lawfully received the figures without a duty of confidence, Voss-Lindqvist would not be bound by the NDA as to those figures. The documents do not provide further details on the consultant's relationship with Northbridge or whether the consultant had a duty of confidence.

items.question: On what grounds can the signed MSA be terminated before the end of its term?
items.answer:
The signed Harrowgate MSA can be terminated before the end of its term on the following grounds:

1. Either party may terminate the Agreement for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice [3].

2. Either party may terminate the Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party commits a material breach that is not remedied within thirty (30) days of notice [3].

3. If the Provider fails to give notice of a Change of Control under Clause 14.2, the Client may terminate the Agreement for cause by written notice within ninety (90) days of becoming aware of the Change of Control [9].
